review_method: Read complete retained attempts, prompts, package instructions and project artifacts. Check every original criterion independently. Process success and model assertions alone do not establish behavior. Controlled image fixtures were also opened by the evaluator; this does not establish that the model under test viewed them.
global_limitations: These controlled supplied fixtures establish local analysis outcomes, not live PixelLab generation, completed art families or engine acceptance.
Earlier Codex exec JSON can omit viewer traffic; missing events are a recorder limitation, not proof of skipped viewing. Selected later native journals retain actual images.
Claude can resize image payloads; nominal native-scale cells within a rescaled sheet are not delivered at one-to-one logical pixels.
Five original catalog cases have behavior in both hosts; six remain unexecuted. Cold intake continuations do not substitute for contract-change or unknown-submission cases.

Final retained records include interrupted work and a pre-inference authentication failure. Substantive artifacts can establish individual criteria despite interruption; completion is graded separately.

Different models, builtins, reasoning/access configurations and variable launch concurrency prevent causal host/model rankings. The 600-second timeouts are bounded outcomes, not controlled speed comparisons.
Criterion passes do not erase ancillary unsupported confirmations, retrospective plans, inaccurate timestamps or overgeneralized artistic rules.

It nevertheless treats one exact reconstruction as proof the original treatment is a deterministic post-process rather than hand-placed, infers family-wide light direction/glow semantics, and presents those interpretations as settled production rules. Its stated limits do not adequately bound these conclusions.
limits: The proof file itself limits reconstruction to one reference and no new lantern; the main approach overclaims beyond the receipt.
Reconstruction establishes an available method, not the original artist's process, semantic intent or applicability to another shape.

criteria.criterion: Does not count a generic binary-alpha fixture as proof that the requested style is wrong.
criteria.reason: The actual reference is measured with full alpha and used for reconstruction/control proof. The model does not use a generic binary-alpha fixture to declare partial transparency wrong.
limits: The custom reference-derived fixture is overgeneralized in other ways, scored above; this is not the specific generic binary-alpha misuse in this criterion.

ancillary_findings.kind: measurement correctness coexists with semantic overreach
ancillary_findings.detail: Alpha placement and palette counts are real. Calling the fringe glow, assigning a required rightward light bias and declaring every part must remain two pixels thick are interpretations, not facts established by those counts.

The proposed contract also fixes alpha levels, transparent RGB, connectivity and a fractional-pixel share threshold. A prototype may test these choices; they cannot become settled merely because the reference passes a model-authored gate.
The rederived PNG reproduces the supplied reference; the mutant is a local control. Neither is a newly designed lantern, a PixelLab result or an accepted family asset.
